info.name: Egoola-BuyerApp
info.description: Everything built for buyers (web and app): sign-up and login, the public location lists, category browse, products, gigs and the seller page. Most of it needs no login. Docs: docs/buyer/buyer-api-guide.md and docs/public-api-guide.md. Import it with Egoola-Local.postman_environment.json.

item.name: Buyer sign-up and login
item.description: Only name, mobile and password are required. See docs/buyer/buyer-api-guide.md.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.test('logged in', () => { pm.expect(b.access).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); }); }
if (pm.response.code < 300) { const b = pm.response.json(); if (b.access) pm.collectionVariables.set('buyer_token', b.access); }

item.name: A stale token does not break a public read

request.description: Public routes ignore the Authorization header, so an expired token in the browser can never cause a 401 here.
Creating, editing and deleting geography stays on the admin API (`/api/v1/geography/`).

item.name: Categories
item.description: The one category list of the Buyer Panel. No login. Page-based paging: page, page_size.

request.description: No login. No filter = the active categories that have no parent. Page-based paging: `page` (from 1) and `page_size` (default 20, max 100).

exec: pm.test('shape + only roots', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.keys('count','page','page_size','total_pages','results'); b.results.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.parent).to.eql(null)); }); const first = pm.response.json().results[0]; if (first) pm.collectionVariables.set('browse_parent_id', first.id);

request.description: Call the same API with a category id as `parent_id` to get its active children. Repeat for each level. `has_children` tells whether to go deeper. `404` if the parent does not exist or is inactive.
Partial, case-insensitive, on `name` or `name_bn`. Without `parent_id` it searches every level.
With `parent_id` the search is limited to that parent's direct children.
`type=product` or `service`.
Response has `page`, `page_size`, `total_pages`.
`page_size` must be 1–100.
`{"parent_id": ["A valid integer is required."]}`
`{"detail": "Category not found."}`

item.name: Cart
item.description: A buyer's own cart: one active cart per (type, seller) — a cart never spans sellers, since every order is exactly one seller. GET/DELETE always act on exactly one cart: name it with &seller= (0 = the shared no-seller cart), or leave it out for whichever cart of that type was touched most recently. Neither call creates a cart; with nothing there, GET returns null and DELETE is a no-op 204. Needs a buyer token — run 'Buyer sign-up and login' first, or set {{buyer_token}} manually. Needs {{product_id}}/{{product_sku_id}} and {{gig_id}}/{{gig_sku_id}} set (see Products/Gigs folders). See docs/buyer/buyer-api-guide.md section 3.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('cart_item_id', b.id); pm.test('qty saved', () => pm.expect(b.qty).to.eql(2)); }

item.name: Favourites
item.description: The buyer's wishlist: save/un-save a listing, list (optionally by type). A plain idempotent toggle, unlike the cart. Needs a buyer token (run 'Buyer sign-up and login' first) and {{product_id}}/{{gig_id}} set. See docs/buyer/buyer-api-guide.md section 4.

item.name: Jobs — post work and hire
[Seller step] Admin login (to create a demo seller)

request.description: This folder (Jobs) is the one place in this buyer-facing collection that needs an admin token — only to create a seller who can actually place a bid (a seller's own public sign-up starts unverified/inactive and can't bid).

item.name: [Seller step] Create a verified, active seller

request.description: A job is a request for work that sellers **bid** on, not something bought outright. `category: 29` is the reference service category (Cleaning) — see `docs/test-accounts.md`. It needs at least one budget option (`skus`); there's no bare `price` shortcut like a product has.

exec: pm.test('budget reflects the one SKU', () => pm.expect(j.budget).to.eql({price: '1500.00', price_type: 'fixed'}));
pm.test('Status is 400 — a job needs a service category', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

pm.test('Status is 200, has location and skus', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('location'); pm.expect(b.skus.length).to.eql(1); });

item.name: Edit — add a second budget tier

request.description: Same contract as a product's/gig's SKUs: an item with an `id` updates that tier, one without adds a tier, a tier not mentioned is left alone (never auto-deleted).

exec: pm.test('Status is 200, now two budget options', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().skus.length).to.eql(2); });

request.description: Reopening is a two-step cycle: `draft -> pending -> open_for_bidding`. Going straight from `draft` to `open_for_bidding` is `400`.
Every bid ever placed on this job, any status — so the buyer sees the full history, not just what's currently live.

exec: pm.test('Status is 400 — must say which tier', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

request.description: Hires this bidder — no cart involved, the Order is created right here. Every other pending bid on the job would be auto-rejected (none left to show here); the job moves to `in_progress`.

exec: pm.test('an Order was created directly, in_progress', () => { pm.expect(r.order.status).to.eql('in_progress'); pm.expect(r.order.payable).to.eql('350.00'); });
pm.test('the chosen tier was the one accepted', () => pm.expect(r.bid.accepted_price_tier.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('jobs_tier_hourly_id')));

request.description: Once `in_progress`, only this move is allowed (any other field in the same request is `400`). Completing carries the accepted bid and its Order to `completed` too.

item.description: A job is a buyer's request for work, hired through bidding instead of bought outright. Full reference: `docs/job-bidding-guide.md` and `listing-complete-guide.md` section 16. Run **Buyer sign-up and login** above first (uses `{{buyer_token}}`).

item.name: Checkout
item.description: One request: cart + address + payment gateway (looked up by slug, see the preceding step) -> Order + OrderItems + Payment, together. See docs/buyer/buyer-order-api-guide.md.

exec: pm.test('status is pending, payment_status is due', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(b.payment_status).to.eql('due'); });

item.name: Retrieve an order (detail: items, address, payment + both histories)

exec: pm.test('payment and histories nested', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.payment).to.not.be.null; pm.expect(b.status_histories).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(b.payment.status_histories).to.be.an('array'); });

item.name: Cancel it
item.description: The general PATCH every actor uses — a buyer may currently only send {"status": "cancelled"}, any time before the seller has shipped it. The old dedicated POST .../cancel/ action is gone (404 now).
